nodes.summary: Let $m$ be an even natural number and let $d_1, \dots, d_m$ be odd natural numbers. If integers $a$ and $b$ with $b \ne 0$ satisfy $a/b = \sum_{i=1}^{m} 1/d_i$, then $a$ is even.
nodes.title: Even sums of odd unit fractions have even numerator

nodes.summary: If $d$ is the odd greedy choice at a rational number $r$, then $1/d \le r$.
nodes.title: The odd greedy unit fraction does not exceed the remainder

nodes.summary: Let $n$ and $d$ be positive natural numbers and let $x_1$ be an odd natural number. Then $x_1$ is the odd greedy choice at $n/d$ (the first denominator of the odd greedy expansion of $n/d$) if and only if $d \le n x_1$ and $n x_1 < d + 2n$, that is, $0 \le n x_1 - d < 2n$ in the integers.
nodes.title: Odd greedy choice at a fraction

nodes.summary: A natural number $d$ is the odd greedy choice at a rational number $r$ if and only if $r > 0$ and $d$ is the least element of the set of positive odd natural numbers $e$ with $1/e \le r$.
nodes.title: Characterization of the odd greedy choice

nodes.summary: For a rational number $r$ and a natural number $d$, $d$ is the odd greedy choice at $r$ when $r > 0$, $d$ is positive and odd, $1/d \le r$, and $d \le e$ for every positive odd natural number $e$ with $1/e \le r$. Equivalently, $1/d$ is the largest unit fraction with odd denominator that does not exceed $r$.
nodes.title: Odd greedy choice

nodes.summary: If $d$ is the odd greedy choice at a rational number $r$, then $d \le e$ for every positive odd natural number $e$ with $1/e \le r$.
nodes.title: The odd greedy choice is minimal

nodes.summary: If $d$ is the odd greedy choice at a rational number $r$, then $d$ is odd.
nodes.title: The odd greedy choice is odd

nodes.summary: If $d$ is the odd greedy choice at a rational number $r$, then $d > 0$.
nodes.title: The odd greedy choice is positive

nodes.summary: If $d$ is the odd greedy choice at a rational number $r$, then $r > 0$.
nodes.title: The odd greedy choice needs a positive remainder

nodes.summary: If $d$ and $d'$ are both odd greedy choices at the same rational number $r$, then $d = d'$.
nodes.title: Uniqueness of the odd greedy choice
